prompt.context: Edoceo is a leading global provider of integrated information solutions to business and professional customers. Customers depend on Edoceo for the information and information applications they need to make the right decisions to run their businesses. Edoceo provides information solutions for professionals across a broad range of industries and disciplines. Edoceo decided to outsource select HR processes including: Recruiting, Benefits Admin, HRIS, HR Admin, L&D, Compensation, Domestic Relocation, Expatriate Admin, Payroll, HR Contact Center. Edoceo is working with one of Deloitte's competitors to implement the outsourcing transition. The initiative's objective is to realize cost savings of 10%-20% of total current annual costs over five years, while maintaining equivalent levels of service. In parallel, Edoceo intends to transform the retained HR organization, creating internal Centers of Excellence (COE) and developing HR Business Partners to support with outsourced services.
prompt.question: Edoceo has hired your team to provide best practice guidance and implementation leadership. How would you design and implement optimal COEs and HR business partner capability for this organization and how would you structure the project? How would you describe a successful outcome for this project?

clarifying_info.q: Why is Edoceo outsourcing these HR functions?
clarifying_info.a: Inefficiency and complexity of the existing HR organization were the driving forces of the outsourcing.

clarifying_info.q: What functions are intended for the COEs?
clarifying_info.a: Benefits, Compensation, Recruiting, Talent Management, HR Decision Support, L&D, Org Development, Diversity, and Policy, Compliance and M&A.

clarifying_info.q: What is the vision for HR Business Partners?
clarifying_info.a: HRBPs will provide business-unit-specific and consultative services to executives and line managers for people-related issues impacting their business unit. Business Partners broker technical talent from the COEs to deliver HR solutions.

clarifying_info.q: Is there a current HRBP role in place?
clarifying_info.a: There is no current assessment of the HRBP role today; each Market Group runs its own entity.

clarifying_info.q: What is the broader transformation context?
clarifying_info.a: Finance and IT are expected to follow a similar outsourcing path. There is significant concern among staff in retained functions about the long-term safety of their jobs.

framework: Plan & Assess: conduct as-is inventory, define COE and Business Partner staffing strategy, establish reporting and metrics strategy, perform stakeholder analysis, conduct change readiness assessment, develop communication and change strategy
Design: design processes for COEs and HR Business Partner roles, build communication, change and training materials, and create detailed implementation plan
Build & Implement: build out process designs and COE structure, deliver training materials for new positions and processes
Support & Integrate: ensure effective interactions with outsourced functions and the larger organization

questions.prompt: How would you structure the project to design and implement optimal COEs and HR Business Partner capability?
questions.guidance: Candidate should propose a phased Plan-Build-Run type approach. Strong answers articulate four phases: (1) Plan & Assess — inventory current state, define staffing strategy for COEs and HRBPs, establish metrics, conduct stakeholder and change readiness analysis, develop communication strategy; (2) Design — process design for COEs and HRBP model, build change and training materials and implementation plan; (3) Build & Implement — execute process designs, build COE structure, deliver training; (4) Support & Integrate — ensure smooth interaction with outsourced vendor and broader organization.

questions.prompt: What does a successful outcome look like for this project?
questions.guidance: Success means achieving 10%-20% cost savings over five years while maintaining equivalent service levels. It also means effective COEs delivering specialized HR services and capable HRBPs acting as consultants to business units. Additional success factors include retained employee confidence/morale, smooth coordination with outsourced functions, and minimal service disruption during transition.

brainstorming.prompt: What else should Edoceo be considering as it implements the outsourcing and development of the COEs?

categories.name: Service Continuity
ideas: Establishing clear SLAs with the outsourcing vendor
Defining escalation paths when outsourced services underperform

categories.name: People and Morale
ideas: Addressing performance and morale issues among retained staff
Communicating clearly about job security in the retained organization
Supporting employees whose roles are being outsourced through transition assistance

categories.name: Talent Retention
ideas: Identifying and retaining key talent in the retained HR organization
Designing attractive career paths within COEs and HRBP roles

categories.name: Change Management
ideas: Robust change management and communication plan for all stakeholders
Training programs for new COE and HRBP roles
Engaging executive sponsors to champion the transformation

categories.name: Linkages to Other Initiatives
ideas: Coordinating HR outsourcing with planned Finance and IT outsourcing initiatives
Ensuring HR transformation aligns with overall corporate strategy
Monitoring interdependencies between outsourced and retained functions

recommendation: Design COEs covering Benefits, Compensation, Recruiting, Talent Management, HR Decision Support, L&D, Org Development, Diversity, and Policy/Compliance/M&A, staffed with deep functional experts
Deploy HR Business Partners embedded in each business unit to broker COE expertise to line managers and executives, replacing the fragmented Market Group model
Implement via a four-phase Plan-Assess-Design-Build-Run approach with clear milestones and governance
risks: Service disruption during the outsourcing transition if handoffs and SLAs are not well-defined
High attrition of retained HR talent due to job insecurity concerns
Poor morale and resistance to change undermining adoption of new COE and HRBP model
Misalignment between outsourced vendor capabilities and retained HR expectations
next_steps: Conduct as-is inventory and change readiness assessment immediately
Define COE staffing strategy and HRBP role profiles
Develop stakeholder communication plan addressing job security concerns
Establish governance and metrics framework to track 10%-20% cost savings target
